seo.title: Karmic tail 18 12 12 compatibility: the Moon and two Hanged Men
seo.description: Karmic tail 18 12 12 compatibility: the Moon at the entry, the Hanged Man twice. Read through Oblomov: Casta Diva, raised bridges and a way out of waiting.

title: Karmic tail 18-12-12 in compatibility: a couple waiting for the bridges
short: The Moon, followed twice by the Hanged Man. The 18-12-12 tail exists only in a couple: two people enter the union through a shared dream that is never said aloud, and then hang between "already" and "not yet". The main task of such a couple is not to love more, but to stop living in the future tense: to choose the person who is here now, not the one they might someday become, and to answer rather than wait.

sections.h2: A song about a secret confided to the moon
paragraphs: Oblomov has not yet met Olga. In the second part of the novel he comes home late one evening, grumbling, puts on his dressing gown, lies down on the sofa and tells Stolz what an ideal day would be like: dinner, guests, the fields. Towards evening "fog hangs over the rye like an upturned sea", lights come on in the house — and here Oblomov starts to sing: "Casta diva... Casta diva! I can't recall Casta diva without being moved... What sorrow there is in those sounds!.. And nobody around knows anything... She is alone... **A secret weighs on her; she confides it to the moon...**"
Stolz replies: "You love that aria? I'm very glad: Olga Ilyinskaya sings it beautifully. I'll introduce you." So this couple's love begins with a song, before the first meeting.

Who is "she", the woman weighed down by a secret? She is Norma from Bellini's opera (1831), a druid priestess. She has secretly broken her vows and borne two children to the Roman proconsul Pollione, and her people know nothing of it. In the scene with the aria the Gauls wait for her signal to rise against Rome. Norma declares that the time has not yet come, cuts the mistletoe and prays to the moon for peace. To herself she admits that she cannot destroy Pollione and wants everything to be as it was. The first lines of the aria:
Casta Diva, che inargenti / queste sacre antiche piante, / a noi volgi il bel sembiante / senza nube e senza vel.
"Chaste goddess, you who silver these sacred ancient trees, turn your fair face to us — without cloud and without veil" (our translation).

The whole tail is already in one aria. A secret union confided to the moon — that is the Moon. A decision put off because "the time has not come" — the Hanged Man. A broken vow and an attachment that can be neither admitted nor broken — the Devil at the centre. And in the same conversation, on the same pages, Stolz invents the word the novel will end on: "Some kind of... Oblomovism" (oblomovshchina). Going off to bed, he says from the doorway: "Now or never — remember!" The name of the chain and the only way out of it are spoken before the heroine has even appeared. And Oblomov sings his aria to the moon lying on the sofa in his dressing gown. The dressing gown is described on the very first page of the novel, and it will turn out to be the third character in this story.

sections.h2: Entry to the task, 18: a love that speaks in hints
paragraphs: The evening when Olga first sings for Oblomov Goncharov sets under the moon, though it takes place in her aunt's drawing room: "They lit a lamp, which shone through the ivy on the trellis like the moon. The dusk hid the outlines of Olga's face and figure and threw something like a crape veil over her; her face was in shadow: all one could hear was a soft but strong voice." At the end of the evening Olga sings Casta diva. Oblomov falls in love with a voice whose face he can barely see.

After that the couple develops a language of its own. Olga picks a sprig of lilac and hands it to him without a word, drops lilies of the valley on the path, Oblomov catches her glances. Goncharov later calls this period "the moment of symbolic hints, meaningful smiles, sprigs of lilac". Oblomov tells Olga that her look seems to say: "I need no words, I can read your looks", and at once admits: "But when you are not there, such a tormenting game of doubts begins." After one meeting he comes home "beaming, as if with 'a crescent moon on his brow', as his nanny used to say", sits down on the sofa and writes in the dust on the table with his finger: "Olga".

The entry point of a couple's tail is what the two want together: shared wishes, agreements, a common language. With this wish the couple enters its task. With 18 the common language is lunar: images, music, hints, signs that only the two understand. It is a real gift. Such couples understand each other from half a word and can build a world no one else can enter. But the entry stands on the line of tasks, and the same wish turns into resistance. What is understood without words never gets said. Such a couple may have a whole dictionary of private jokes and songs, while the question "what are we to each other" or "are we living together" is never asked once. The plan exists as a mood.

The funniest thing is that Oblomov had described the wife of his dreams in advance, and the description has the line: "No moon, no sadness needed." He wanted a love without the moon and fell for a voice singing to the moon.

The entry holds an arithmetic clue as well. The couple's M point is the sum of the two partners' M points, and for the 18-12-12 tail it is always made as 9 + 9: each partner's personal tail begins with the Hermit. Two habits of living inside oneself, added together, give the Moon. The couple builds a shared inner world, like a second room for two with its own language. Only that room is also easy to lock oneself into.

sections.h2: A light that gives no warmth
paragraphs: Both lovers in the novel describe their love, and both with the same image — reflected light. Of Olga the author writes: "She weighed her power over him in an instant, and she liked this role of a guiding star, a ray of light that she would pour over a stagnant lake and that would be reflected in it." Oblomov, in a letter, describes her love as "an unconscious need to love which, for want of real nourishment, for want of fire, burns with a false light that gives no warmth".

Each sees a mirror in the other. Olga sees in Oblomov a lake in which her light will be reflected. Oblomov sees in her love a light that does not warm. Moonlight is not its own but reflected — one of Waite's best-known thoughts about the Moon — and in the novel it is the lovers themselves who say it. Benebell Wen adds one more trait to the Moon that fits this couple well: "There is a strong theme of **conservation in the card, rather than exploration or expansion**", "a sense of needing to feel protected, and thus forming the tough outer shell", and at the same time "a profound vulnerability that the Seeker is trying to conceal from others". Oblomov's shell is the dressing gown and the sofa. Olga's shell is pride and her role.

The most precise passage in the novel is the letter Oblomov writes after a sleepless night to break things off while it is not too late. He warns Olga: "You are mistaken; the man before you is not the one you were waiting for, the one you dreamed of. Wait — he will come, and then you will wake up." And the key sentence: **"your present 'I love you' is not real love but future love"**.

This is the trap of the lunar entry: love for a future image. A few months later Olga says the same thing in her own words: "I loved the future Oblomov!" Later still Stolz reads the letter aloud and sums it up: "You had parted even before you separated, and you were faithful not to love but to its ghost, which you had invented yourselves — that is the whole secret." The letter turned out to be a prophecy. The last word in Waite's divinatory list for the Hanged Man is precisely "prophecy".

That same day in the park, in a conversation about the letter, the Hanged Man appears too. Oblomov asks: "Am I not giving you up because I foresee your happiness ahead, because I am sacrificing myself to it?" Olga answers that he hid in the bushes to see whether she would cry: "this is not love, this is..." — "Selfishness!" Oblomov finishes himself. In the same list Waite gives the Hanged Man "sacrifice", and in the reversed position "selfishness". Here that pair of words is acted out in person.

sections.h2: Middle of the task, 12: "Katya, have they put the bridges back?"
paragraphs: Summer is ending, and love, in Goncharov's words, "began to turn into some kind of duty; mutual rights appeared". The couple is secretly engaged. Olga's aunt has been told nothing, and Oblomov is waiting for a letter from his estate, for money and for a flat. Meanwhile the servants give the secret away. Zakhar asks his master when the wedding is and explains how he found out: "Katya told Semyon, Semyon told Nikita, Nikita told Vasilisa, Vasilisa told Anisya, and Anisya told me..." Oblomov is horrified: "Olga kept silent, I didn't dare even think aloud, and in the servants' hall they've settled everything!" — and he shouts at Zakhar that it is all "nonsense, absurdity, lies, calumny". Waite's list for the Moon has exactly that word, calumny. A lunar couple is secretive even when all is well, and that is why rumours grow around it.

Then autumn comes. Oblomov lives on the Vyborg Side, Olga on the other bank of the Neva. "The bridges had already been taken up, and the Neva was about to freeze." He could cross over and stay closer to Olga, and Oblomov even puts his feet on the floor, "but, after thinking a little, with a careworn face and a sigh, slowly lay down again in his place". He hides from the servant Olga has sent and replies by note that he is unwell. The book she sent him he put down open at page 105, face down, and there it has lain for several days. Every morning the first thing he asks is whether the bridges are back.
And here Goncharov makes the move that makes the novel worth rereading:
"Katya, have they put the bridges back?" Olga asked her maid, waking up that same morning. And the question was repeated every day. Oblomov had no idea of it.

This is the middle of the tail. Two people wait for the same bridge, each on their own bank. There is not one idler here: both are hanging, and each waits for the other to cross the river. The N point shows how the couple lives the way from the wish to the task. For 18-12-12 that way runs through a pause: "And he was still at the same point of being unable to move forward."

There is a numerical clue too. If 18-12-12 were a personal tail, the middle would be counted from the ends: 18 + 12 = 30, 3 + 0 = 3, the Empress. In a couple the middle is added up from the two partners' middles, and here it is always 9 + 3 = 12. Where personal logic would put the Empress — home, wedding, children — the couple has the Hanged Man. A personal matrix never has such a middle at all. The Empress is exactly what Oblomov saw in his dreams: a bride "at the altar, with a long veil, then at the head of the marriage bed... and at last a mother among a group of children". The picture of home stays a picture, and the life between the dream and the home hangs.

In a couple today it looks quite ordinary. The wedding date floats: "after the renovation". Meeting the parents is put off "until the holidays", moving in "until the lease runs out". Each secretly checks whether the other has already crossed. According to Lisovskaya, couples with the twelfth energy get going slowly, and they often need a push from outside to marry. In the novel the push came from the servants' gossip, only it did not push — it froze.

sections.h2: Main task, 12: "I am waiting not for assurances of love but for a short answer"
paragraphs: The main point of a couple's tail is read mostly through difficulties: what the two cannot manage and what they have to learn. Goncharov gives a whole scene to this at the end of the third part. Some remember it as a break-up, but it is built as an exam on the main task.

Olga begins with a confession: "I thought I would bring you back to life, that you could still live for me — but you died long ago." And she adds: "A stone would have come to life from what I did." Oblomov answers with what their whole middle rested on: "But perhaps..." — and hesitantly adds: "in a year..." Olga gives him one more chance: "If you say yes boldly and after thinking it over, I take back my decision: here is my hand, and let us go wherever you like — abroad, to the country, even to the Vyborg Side!" He begins: "If only you knew how I love..." And then Olga says the key line of the tail: **"I am waiting not for assurances of love but for a short answer."**
When everything has already been decided, Oblomov finds the right words: "Take me as I am, love what is good in me." Olga shakes her head, and a little later says: "I loved the future Oblomov!"

It is easy to read this scene as a verdict on one of the two, but a couple's tail describes the task of both. Olga holds the union up with all her strength, puts a summer, her pride and her reputation into it, and gets postponements in return. Oblomov is tormented by guilt and hides deeper. According to Lisovskaya, this is what the Hanged Man looks like in the main task: one partner carries the relationship and gets reproaches, there are no shared goals, expectations of the partner are too high. Only here both are hanging. Olga is suspended on the project of bringing him back to life, Oblomov on the hope that someday he will be ready. Both love a future person: she loves the future Oblomov, he loves his future self.

Waite has a sentence about the Hanged Man that most retellings pass by: "He who can understand that the story of his higher nature is imbedded in this symbolism will receive intimations concerning a great awakening that is possible". The awakening is promised to the one who has understood his own story, not to the one who tries to wake someone else. Olga was wrong not in her feeling but in her craft: no one can be woken from the outside, not even by a voice singing Casta diva.

The couple's main task is made up of the partners' main tasks: one has the Moon, 18, in this place of the personal tail, the other has the World, 21. Together 39, 3 + 9 = 12. Fog plus a hunger for the whole world gives suspension. In one sentence of Olga's both halves of this sum can be heard: "this is not enough for me, I need something more, and what — I don't know!"

In a couple today the task sounds like this. One books, explains, suggests, waits, gets tired and starts to reproach. The other answers "let's see", feels guilty and withdraws even further. A year later both are surprised that "nothing happened", though the main thing did: the decision was never made.

sections.h2: The atmosphere inside the couple, 15: a chain neither of the two owns
paragraphs: The centre of a couple's chart is the atmosphere of the union, what is between the two when nobody is watching. Every couple with the 18-12-12 tail has 15, the Devil, at the centre. There are no exceptions: the centre is added up from the partners' centres, and with this tail they are always 9 and 6, the Hermit and the Lovers. One more clue: no birth date ever gives 15 at the centre of a personal matrix. Neither of the two brings this chain. It appears only when a hermit and a lover sit down side by side.

Goncharov describes this atmosphere without any cards. In such a "comedy or tragedy", he writes, the two almost always have the same roles: **"of the tormentor, male or female, and the victim"**. Of Olga it is said that she "triumphed in her primacy in this duel in all sorts of ways". Olga tells Oblomov: "What I have once called mine I will not give back, unless it is taken from me." And Oblomov, in his letter, fears something else: "And what will happen when I become attached... How will I tear myself away then?" One holds on by power, the other by dependence, and both are chained.

But this couple has a third character as well. Back in summer, in the park, Olga asks: "if not even another woman, but your dressing gown becomes dearer to you?" On the night after the break-up Oblomov comes home, and Goncharov ends the chapter with a single object: Zakhar undressed him, pulled off his boots "and threw over him — the dressing gown!" The Devil at the centre of this couple is not a wicked partner. It is whatever each holds dearer than the other: comfort, pride, the role of rescuer, "the way it was". Wen writes that "The Devil is not a literal beast or demon; The Devil personifies human selfishness", and speaks of a **"preference for instant gratification over delayed gratification"**. The dressing gown is the instant gratification. The delayed one is the road to Olga across the river.

Olga's last question in that scene sounds like an incantation: "Who cursed you, Ilya? What have you done?.. What has ruined you? There is no name for this evil..." — "There is," he answers barely audibly, and to her questioning look whispers: "Oblomovism!" The evil gets a name, and it is the name not of a person but of a way of living. Wen specifically notes that "The Devil card does not necessarily mean the Seeker is entirely to blame". The guilt in this couple does not split into "him" and "her": the chain is shared.

In Waite's divinatory list the Devil has a clause that fits the fact "every couple, without exception": "that which is predestined but is not for this reason evil". And the description of the card says that the one exalted above the chained figures "is not to be their master for ever". In Lisovskaya the conclusion about the fifteenth energy in a couple is that **no one belongs to anyone**. For this couple it is not a moral but a technique: the chain weakens when it is named aloud.

sections.h2: The couple's values: the peace that comes after the road
paragraphs: The couple's values are what the union exists for. Couples with the 18-12-12 tail have two cards here: the Hermit in 76.3% and the Moon in 23.7%.

The Hermit among the values means quiet, depth, unhurriedness, honesty. In the novel Stolz names them when he explains to Olga what she still loves in Oblomov: "an honest, faithful heart! That is his natural gold", and, remembering himself, adds "dove-like tenderness". In itself this is no vice. Oblomov dreamed of a wife "as peace itself", and there is nothing shameful in that dream.

The difference lies in when the peace comes. Wen's Hermit is a man who "has been on a long journey" and at the end of it "has found peace". Oblomov wanted peace instead of the journey: when Stolz suggests leaving in two weeks, he answers "perhaps in three months or so". For a couple with this tail quiet is a real value, only it should be the quiet of a hermit who has arrived, not the quiet of a sofa nobody ever got up from.

In one such couple in four the values hold the Moon. Then the union exists for the dream itself: shared poetry, a secret world of their own, music for two. That is a value too, but it is easy to spend it on hiding.

sections.h2: The way out: into the moonlight, face to face
paragraphs: In the fourth part Olga is married to Stolz. She is tormented by a strange sadness, which she hides. One evening they are walking along an avenue of poplars, and Goncharov writes: "He led her out of the avenue and turned her face to the moonlight. 'Look at me!'" For the first time Olga names aloud what troubles her. A few turns of the avenue later she, "in her turn, led him out into the moonlight and looked questioningly into his eyes". Stolz explains to her: "This is the sadness of a soul questioning life about its secret", and suggests: "we will bow our heads and humbly live through the difficult moment".

This is the very request of Casta diva, finally granted: to turn one's face to the other "without cloud and without veil". The moon is the same as at the start of the novel. The difference is that the two stand in its light face to face and say aloud what used to be a hint. The Hanged Man is here too, but chosen: to bow their heads together for a difficult moment is a pause the two take together, not a hook on which each hangs alone.

The novel gives Olga a different husband, but a couple's tail does not advise changing partners. It speaks about what these two should do. Translated into the language of the tail, the novel's hints come out like this.

ul: **Turn hints into sentences.** A sprig of lilac is lovely, but the sentence "I want us to live together" is stronger. The Moon at its best is a couple that can talk about feelings and does not invent things on the other's behalf.
**Give a short answer.** A date, a decision or an honest "no" instead of "in a year". A pause is good when it has an end and both have chosen it.
**Love the one who is there.** "Take me as I am" — the partner is not a draft of a future person. A project of bringing someone else back to life is a beautiful form of the same chain.

**Find the third at the centre and name it.** Whatever each holds dearer than the other: the dressing gown, the role of rescuer, pride, "the way it was". A chain that has been named holds less tightly.
**Each crosses their own bridge.** No one can wake the other; one can wake up oneself and hold out a hand from the other bank.

paragraphs: And a last clue, from the author's life. The novel about a suspended life was itself suspended for a long time. Goncharov conceived it in 1847, published "Oblomov's Dream" separately, then broke off for years and sailed on the frigate Pallada. In the summer of 1857, in Marienbad, he finished three parts in a few weeks. A pause after which a whole thing ripens is the Hanged Man too. That is the side of the card for whose sake a couple with this tail is worth learning to wait differently.

sections.h2: How the 18-12-12 tail comes about: an example with two dates
paragraphs: Each point of a couple's chart is the sum of the same points of the two personal matrices, reduced to 22. Take the dates 11.02.1976 and 02.01.1980.

ul: the 18-12-12 tail occurs in roughly one couple in 929 (0.108%), 81st place out of 97 couples' tails;
it is made by only one combination of personal tails: 9-9-18 in one partner and 9-3-21 in the other;
so the couple's centre is always 15, and the values are 9 or 18;
there are no other couples' tails from these numbers: the couple calculation never gives 12-18-12 or 12-12-18, and there is no personal tail 18-12-12.

intro: The three numbers of a couple's tail are read in order, and each has its own role.

ul: **18, The Moon — entry to the task.** What the couple wants together and the language in which they agree. Here it is a language of half-tones: songs, hints, private words, a secret for two. The wish is there, but it lives in the imagination, not in words.

**12, The Hanged Man — middle of the task.** How the couple moves from the wish to the task: through a pause. Moving in, the wedding, meeting the family — all "a little later", and each quietly waits for the other to move first.

**12, The Hanged Man — main task.** What the couple has to learn: to take the union off the hook of waiting. Not to wait until the partner becomes the person they imagined, but to choose them as they are today — or honestly say "no".

intro: The strangest thing about this triple is the repeat. The pause the couple walks through is its main task as well: the middle and the end of the tail are the same card. And at the centre of the chart every such couple has the Devil, the card of attachment, which no personal destiny matrix ever has at its centre. Neither of the two brings it: it is born only between them.

Russian literature knows this plot almost by heart, though it is usually read as the story of one idle man. In fact it is the story of a couple. Ivan Goncharov, Oblomov, 1859: Ilya Ilyich Oblomov and Olga Ilyinskaya. (Quotations from the novel here are our own translations from the Russian.)

faq.q: What does the karmic tail 18-12-12 mean in compatibility?
faq.a: These are the couple's tasks, not a personal programme of one partner. The Moon at the entry: the couple comes together through a shared dream and a language of hints. The Hanged Man in the middle: the way to the goal runs through pauses and postponements. The Hanged Man as the main task: learning to step out of waiting, to choose the partner as they are today and to answer briefly.

faq.q: Why does the Hanged Man appear twice in this tail?
faq.a: A repeat does not double the card; each point has its own role. In the middle the Hanged Man describes how the couple lives: through a pause. In the main task it describes what to learn: to manage that pause so that it is chosen and has an end, rather than turning into a hook.

faq.q: Does the 18-12-12 tail occur in a personal destiny matrix?
faq.a: No. In a personal matrix the middle of the tail is derived from the ends, and with ends 18 and 12 it would be 3. In a couple the middle is added up from the two partners' middles, so 18-12-12 occurs only in a couple.

faq.q: Does the 18-12-12 tail mean the couple is doomed to wait or to part?
faq.a: No. The tail does not predict events or dates; it shows where the couple easily gets stuck and what to learn. Goncharov's novel is one version of this plot; the scene of Olga and Stolz in the moonlight shows the same Moon and the same Hanged Man at their best.

faq.q: How can you tell a couple has the 18-12-12 tail without a calculator?
faq.a: Look at the partners' personal karmic tails: one must have 9-9-18, the other 9-3-21. This couple's tail cannot be made any other way. The most reliable way is to calculate the couple's chart in the compatibility calculator.

A secret union confided to the moon, a decision put off until later, a bond that can be neither admitted nor broken — the whole tail is already in one aria. Stolz replies that Olga Ilyinskaya sings this aria beautifully.

Oblomov whispers: "Oblomovism!" The evil gets a name, and it is the name not of a person but of a way of living. **The chain weakens when it is named aloud**: no one belongs to anyone.

report.h3: The way out: face to face in the moonlight

report: In the last part Olga, now married to Stolz, hides a strange sadness. One evening on a walk "he led her out of the avenue and turned her face to the moonlight. 'Look at me!'" A few turns later she, "in her turn, led him out into the moonlight and looked questioningly into his eyes". This is the request of Casta diva, finally granted: to turn one's face "without cloud and without veil". The moon is the same as at the start. The difference is that the two stand in its light face to face and say aloud what used to be a hint. The Hanged Man is still here, only chosen: "we will bow our heads and humbly live through the difficult moment".
A couple's tail does not advise changing partners. It suggests something else to these two:

ul: give a short answer: a date, a decision or an honest "no" instead of "in a year";
love the one who is there, not a draft of a future person;
find what each holds dearer than the other, and name it;
each crosses their own bridge: no one can wake the other; one can wake up oneself and hold out a hand from the other bank.

report: A pause is good when it has an end and both have chosen it.
